speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Susanna's hand is better than thine when thou art in a hurry. I set her a bill for Joan, and she ruled it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: She ruled mine, on Thursday, and was right. I'll write her sentence fair. Not with a blot in it for her to correct.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The twins' school-shoes are through at the toe. Both. I measured them against each other, and they have agreed to wear out as a pair.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I'll put shoes in the Christmas pack, then. Say the size as thou said the bill, and I won't guess it from London.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: I'll say it to Hobbins when he is next in, if thou art on a stage. Don't buy a pair because they looked like a kindness.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Joan. We said we would talk of Joan, and we have talked of shoes.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Joan will marry when she means to, and not when a table is dull. She told me so in the kitchen, without asking either of us to arrange it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Good. I have arranged enough for one night, and all of it was a refusal.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Thou refused Edmund a life he has not earned. That is not the same as refusing a sister her own mind.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No. She can have a mind. He can have a shop, until he has more than an admiration.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Sit a little longer. The bench smells of chamomile, and the road will not.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A little longer. Then the book, and then sleep, and then six.
